question: The Jagannath Temple in Puri is an example of which style of architecture?
solution: The correct answer is __**Nagara (Kalinga)**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Jagannath Temple** in Puri is an example of the **Nagara style of architecture**, specifically the **Kalinga sub-style**, which is prevalent in Odisha. • The Nagara style is characterized by its **curvilinear tower (Shikhara)**, often adorned with intricate carvings and sculptures, commonly found in northern and eastern India. • The **Kalinga sub-style** is a distinct variation of Nagara architecture, featuring a **rekha deula (curvilinear tower), pidha deula (pyramidal roof), and khakhara deula (wagon-shaped roof)**. • The **Jagannath Temple** was built in the 12th century by King **Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva** of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty. • The temple complex includes structures such as the **Main Shrine (Vimana), Jagamohana (Audience Hall), Natamandapa (Dance Hall), and Bhoga Mandapa (Offering Hall)**, showcasing the distinct elements of Kalinga architecture.
